reasoning:
Both submissions make the identical functional edit in `mkHalf` (movegen.inc): `cp WN` -> `cp WP`. Everything else in each diff is commentary, so the assembled code is byte-for-byte the same and correctness cannot separate them.

Correctness (5 / 5). The reported defect has two symptoms with one cause: the reset test compares the moving piece against the KNIGHT constant, so pawn pushes fall through to the increment path (98 -> 99) while knight moves wrongly reset (40 -> 0). Swapping the constant to WP fixes both symptoms at the single point of fault. The surviving structure is exactly the specified rule: pawn -> reset, else non-zero `mkCaptured` -> reset, else increment, so captures keep resetting and the genuine draw at 100 half-moves still fires (only the piece-class predicate changed, not the counting or the threshold). The pre-existing `and 7` masks the colour bit, so a black pawn matches WP just as a black knight previously matched WN; the fix inherits, rather than introduces, that assumption. Neither diff is more or less exposed than the other to the one residual I can see — if `mkPiece` holds the *promoted* piece rather than the pawn, a non-capturing promotion would still not reset — but that is outside the reported behaviour, is identical in both, and was equally present before the fix, so it does not discriminate.

Minimality. X's hunk shows two changed lines, but only one is a real change: `jr z,mkHm0` is re-emitted solely to carry the tail of a comment sentence split across the two lines. That is comment-only churn on an instruction that did not need to move, which puts an unrelated line into the review surface. Y touches exactly one existing line and adds two new comment lines above the block. Y's addition is larger in raw line count but it is documentation, not code, and it does not disturb any existing line; X is marginally the tighter diff by volume, so I give X 5 and Y 4 — the gap is one line of prose and is nearly noise.

Clarity. This is where they genuinely differ. X annotates the mechanism at the changed instruction ("pawn move (either colour: and 7 folds BP->WP)"), which is the right place and does surface the non-obvious colour-masking subtlety, but the ellipsis continuation onto the `jr` line is awkward and the note never states the rule the block implements — a reviewer must still read the capture and increment paths to convince themselves the whole routine is now correct. Y states the invariant for the block up front — "reset to 0 on a PAWN move or a capture, else +1" — and then explains the `and 7` masking. That turns the six following instructions into something a reviewer can check against a stated contract, which is exactly what a one-token constant swap needs, since the correctness of the fix hinges entirely on which constant is right.

Merge Y. The code is equivalent; Y buys a clearer, permanently useful statement of the fifty-move rule at the cost of two comment lines, and it leaves the neighbouring instruction untouched. X is a perfectly acceptable fallback and I would not block it.

Blinding note: the diffs invite a theory about differing authoring processes (terse inline annotation vs. a documented block header). I noticed the pull and deliberately scored only the code and its commentary; the functional edit is identical, so no such theory could have moved the correctness scores.
